ancestry_handling: All cohort-level analyses restricted to European-genetic-ancestry individuals passing cohort QC (genetic outliers removed); EduYears measured at age >=30. UKB European ancestry for EA4 X-chromosome work = self-report White/British/Irish/other white AND loading >0 on UKB PC1 (Supp Note s3.1.1); the autosomal UKB sample definition is not separately restated. Relatedness: cohort-specific (EA3 Supp Table 19 records which cohorts used mixed models); for the UKB autosomal GWAS the software/relatedness handling is not stated explicitly in the sources checked (main text says UKB GWAS used methodology identical to Lee et al. 2018; Supp Note s3.1.1 implies the X-chromosome analysis departed from EA3 by using BOLT-LMM with relatives instead of Plink1.9 on unrelateds).
phenotype_preprocessing: EduYears: highest qualification mapped to ISCED 1997 category, then to a years-of-schooling equivalent. EA4 recoded UKB NVQ/HND/HNC holders from 19 years to (age left full-time education - 5), dropping those leaving before age 12 (Supp Note s1.1). UKB: EduYears residualised on first 40 UKB PCs, a third-degree polynomial in birth year (sex and interactions per EA3 spec) and genotype-measurement batch indicators (Supp Note s3.1.1, stated as same as autosomal UKB analysis). Released betas are per SD of EA (Extended Data Fig. 3 legend: phenotype standardised to unit variance).
association_model_covariates: Common cohort specification (Supp Note s2.2.4; EA3 Supp Note s1.5): EduYears ~ SNP + first 10 PCs + standardised controls [third-order polynomial in year of birth, female indicator, their interactions] + study-specific controls. UKB: 40 UKB PCs, cubic birth year (+ sex and interactions), batch dummies (via residualisation). 23andMe (not in this public file): age instead of birth year plus genotype-batch controls. Software varied by cohort (EA3 Supp Table 19).
meta_analysis: Sample-size-weighted meta-analysis (METAL) of Lee 2018 cohorts excl. 23andMe and UKB (N=324,162) + new UKB GWAS (N=441,121) [+23andMe in the restricted full meta]; SEs inflated by sqrt(LDSC intercept). Covariates varied by cohort beyond the common specification.

ancestry_handling: Restricted to 1KG-EUR-like individuals. At least the top 15 genetic PCs per cohort. Male and female samples analysed separately; MTAG used when combining sexes to account for potential sample overlap/relatedness between male and female samples. No further LDSC-intercept correction after MTAG. Relatedness handling within cohorts (e.g. mixed model) not stated in main text.
phenotype_preprocessing: Natural-log-transformed income measures. Sample limited to people not enrolled in education at survey, or aged >30 if enrolment unknown. Measure definitions in Supp Info s2.1 and Supp Tables 1-2 (not accessed). MTAG outputs standardised effect sizes (betas per SD of the Income Factor).
association_model_covariates: Per cohort and sex: log income ~ SNP + hours worked (with square and cube), year of survey, employment-status indicators (e.g. retired, unemployed), self-employment, pension benefits (as available; Supp Table 4) + at least the top 15 PCs + cohort-specific genotyping batch/platform covariates. Inflation, business cycle and age effects handled with dummy variables at cohort level (preregistered plan, osf.io/rg8sh s6). Covariates varied by cohort according to data availability.
meta_analysis: Per income measure and sex: sample-size-weighted METAL across 32 cohorts; sexes combined with meta-analysis MTAG; four measures combined into the Income Factor with MTAG (heritabilities allowed to differ). EasyQC on cohort files.
sources_checked: Kweon 2025 Nat Hum Behav doi:10.1038/s41562-024-02080-7: Results p.795 (PDF p2), Methods "GWAS meta-analysis" (PDF p8); preregistration osf.io/rg8sh referenced but not opened; Supplementary Information and Supp Tables 1-4 not accessed.
notes: Exact age terms, PC count beyond the minimum of 15, and relatedness handling per cohort sit in Supp Table 4/Supp Info (not accessed). UKB contributes household and occupational income.

role: Exposure, primary (all ancestries; EUR-only file as sensitivity)
ancestry_handling: Individuals assigned to genetic ancestry groups by projecting UKB onto PCs of 1000 Genomes + HGDP and a random-forest classifier (top 6 reference PCs, probability >0.5), then ancestry outliers pruned by centroid distance. Within each ancestry group: PC-Relate (k=10) and maximal unrelated set used to compute ancestry-specific PCs; related individuals projected and retained; SAIGE mixed model with kinship random effect accounts for relatedness. GWAS run separately per ancestry group. For TDI the meta includes EUR 420,035, CSA 8,864, AFR 6,624, EAS 2,698, AMR 977 (MID failed QC per project SOURCES.md). The EUR-only analysis = beta_EUR/se_EUR columns of the same file (EUR-group SAIGE GWAS).
phenotype_preprocessing: Continuous trait processed through PHESANT, which applied inverse-rank normal transformation within each ancestry group (betas in SD units of IRNT TDI).
association_model_covariates: SAIGE linear mixed model (kinship random effect) with fixed covariates: age, sex, age*sex, age^2, age^2*sex, first 10 (ancestry-specific) PCs. Same covariates for every ancestry group; no assessment centre or array covariates listed.
meta_analysis: Inverse-variance-weighted meta-analysis across the within-ancestry GWAS (beta_meta). Covariates identical across ancestry groups.

ancestry_handling: UKB inputs: self-reported white participants within mean +/-3 SD on first six genotype PCs, plus sample QC (sex concordance, heterozygosity/missingness, call rate >0.9). Relatedness and structure in UKB GWAS handled by REGENIE whole-genome regression (LOCO). Factor GWAS inherits ancestry handling of inputs; EUR only.
phenotype_preprocessing: Factor GWAS has no phenotype of its own: Genomic SEM single common factor fitted to LDSC genetic covariance of four input GWAS; multivariate GWAS (MAF>0.01, INFO>0.6) gives per-SNP gSES effects and heterogeneity Q. Inputs: (1) occupational prestige = CAMSIS from UKB job code (field 20277) per Akimova method, own UKB GWAS N=279,644; (2) household income = own UKB GWAS of 5-level HI (N=379,598) meta-analysed (METAL, sample-size weighted) with Kweon 2025 income excl. UKB (MTAG-combined, Neff 402,029) -> N=781,627; (3) EA = own UKB GWAS of binary university degree (N=428,990, Firth logistic) meta-analysed with SSGAC EA3 EduYears excl. UKB/23andMe (N=324,162) -> N=753,152; (4) Townsend deprivation (own UKB GWAS, N=440,350), sign flipped so higher = higher SES. Transformations (e.g. IRNT) of the UKB input phenotypes not stated.
association_model_covariates: No association covariates of its own (multivariate summary-statistic model). UKB input GWAS (REGENIE v3.1.3, both steps): sex, age at assessment, assessment centre, genotyping array, genotyping batch, first 40 PCs. External inputs carry their own covariates (Lee 2018; Kweon 2025 - varied by cohort).
meta_analysis: Input-level: METAL sample-size-weighted meta for HI and EA (UKB + SSGAC), beta/SE reconstructed from Z (Zhu et al. formula). Factor-level: Genomic SEM (v0.0.5c), which models sample overlap via LDSC cross-trait intercepts. Effective N=947,466.
sources_checked: Xia 2025 Mol Psychiatry doi:10.1038/s41380-025-03047-4: Methods "Samples", "Measures", "Genome-wide association studies", "Phenotypic and genomic structural equation modelling", "Meta analysis of income and education", "Replication data sets" (PDF p2-5), Table 1, Code availability; GWAS Catalog GCST90566708 metadata (gses_xia2025_meta.yaml).

ancestry_handling: Ten de novo studies, all listed as European ancestry except MGB Biobank 'Predominantly European ancestry (95%)' and UK Biobank listed as '~95% European ancestry' in Suppl. Table 1; the UKB study description (Suppl. Note p.11) states the GWAS used 472,335 individuals 'of European ancestry'. Ancestry adjustment by study-specific PCs (see model). Relatedness: UKB and HUNT used SAIGE logistic mixed models; EPIC-CVD, Greek cohort, MGB and TIMI excluded first/second-degree relatives; GerMIFS5/6 excluded relatives; GerMIFS7 excluded PI_HAT>=0.125 (Suppl. Table 1 'Sample filters'). Combined with previously published CARDIoGRAMplusC4D summary statistics (predominantly European).
phenotype_preprocessing: Binary CAD; case/control definitions per study (Suppl. Table 1). UKB cases: prevalent or incident MI or intervention (CABG, PTCA) from Hospital Episode Statistics or self-report, or IHD death from ONS; controls CAD- and angina-free. EPIC-CVD/GerMIFS: prevalent or incident CAD ICD-10 I20-I25; deCODE: ICD-9/10 or NCSP procedure codes; HUNT and MGB: prevalent+incident 'CAD intermediate' code sets (I21-I25 plus ICD-9 / CPT procedure codes); Greek: ACS or left main CAD; TIMI: established CAD. MI share of cases ranged 9%-100% across studies. No transformation (binary trait).
association_model_covariates: Per-study additive logistic (or logistic mixed) models of CAD 'adjusting for study-specific covariates, including those accounting for potential ancestry effects' (Methods). Covariates by study (Suppl. Table 1): UK Biobank - genotyping array, birth year, sex, PCs 1-5, SAIGE v26/27/29 (logistic mixed model); HUNT - array, PC1-4, birth year, sex, SAIGE v29.1; deCODE - county of origin, deCODE software; EPIC-CVD - recruitment centre, array, PCs 1-10, SNPTEST; GerMIFS5/6/7 - 5 PCs, SNPTEST; Greek CAD cohort - PCs 1-4, SNPTEST; MGB Biobank - PCs 1-5, PLINK2; TIMI - sex, age, history of AF, history of diabetes, imputation batch, PCs 1-5, PLINK2. Age and sex were therefore NOT uniformly included (e.g., GerMIFS, MGB, EPIC-CVD, Greek list PCs/centre only). Covariates of the previously published CARDIoGRAMplusC4D summary statistics are not restated in Aragam 2022.
meta_analysis: Fixed-effect inverse-variance-weighted meta-analysis in METAL of the 10 de novo studies plus prior CARDIoGRAMplusC4D summary statistics (variant-specific sample-size maximisation; variant filtering in Suppl. Note); 20,073,070 variants. Covariates varied by cohort.
sources_checked: Aragam 2022 Nat Genet doi:10.1038/s41588-022-01233-6: Methods 'Genetic discovery meta-analysis' and 'Cross-ancestry comparison' (p.14-15); Supplementary Note p.1-2 & UK Biobank study description (p.11) (41588_2022_1233_MOESM1_ESM.pdf); Supplementary Table 1 rows 'Ancestry','Cases','Controls','Sample filters','Covariates','Software' (MOESM4_ESM.xlsx sheet ST1)
notes: Study-level covariate sets are heterogeneous; several studies did not adjust for age/sex. UKB is included (sample overlap with UKB-based exposure GWAS). The CARDIoGRAMplusC4D component covariates were not re-checked in their original papers.

association_model_covariates: European studies as in cad_aragam2022_eur (study-specific covariates, Suppl. Table 1). ancestry_handling: Population-stratified analysis by genetically inferred ancestry (GIA). Published SM (PDF p.2, 'Population assignment'): 1000 Genomes reference merged with MVP; EIGENSOFT smartpca used to project reference PC loadings; random-forest classifier trained on top 10 reference PCs; individuals assigned to a group if probability >50%, others excluded. Main text p.10 (limitations): the 50% threshold excluded 5,953 participants (<1% of cohort); authors note this may neglect admixture. Groups: AFR, AMR, EAS, EUR (SAS too few cases). Parallel HARE-based GWAS also run (SM p.3) - not the files used here (file N matches GIA Table S2). GWAS run separately within each GIA group; relatedness handled within SAIGE GLMM (SM p.4 'to account for participant relatedness and unbalanced case-control ratios'); SAIGE-GPU builds a full GRM (ref. 48 title); no relative-exclusion step described. PCs: 'PC1-10' selected for adjustment (SM p.2), population-specific (SM p.4). This file: EUR GIA group (Table S1 EUR N=449,042).
phenotype_preprocessing: Binary phecode from VA EHR ICD-9/ICD-10 codes, follow-up to September 2020 (SM p.2). Published SM p.3 ('Phenotypes from ICD codes'): ICD-9 and ICD-10 codes mapped to 1,876 phecodes (Bastarache 2021, SM ref. 62); case = at least two phecode-mapped ICD-9/ICD-10 codes; control = no instance of a phecode-mapped code; >=200 cases required within each population group; VA-protected conditions (e.g., sickle cell anaemia, HIV) excluded. Table S2: Phe_411 'Ischemic Heart Disease', cases 141,465 / controls 275,809 (N 417,274) - identical to num_cases/num_controls in our downloaded file. Individuals with exactly one mapped code are by construction neither case nor control. Phecode exclusion ranges for controls are not described; phecode map version (e.g., 1.2 vs X) is not stated. Age definition (enrolment vs last visit) not stated. No transformation (binary).
association_model_covariates: SAIGE (GPU-optimised SAIGE-GPU on OLCF Summit; SM p.4) generalized/logistic mixed model: step 1 on directly genotyped variants, step 2 on imputed dosages (hybrid African Genome Resources + 1000G Phase 3 v5 panel; SM p.2). Variants included: imputation quality >0.3 and MAC >40 within the population group (SM p.4; main text p.3 '>44.3M variants [with minor allele count (MAC) > 40]'). Covariates: 'Analyses were adjusted for age, sex, and ten population-specific genetic PCs' (SM p.4); limitations (main p.10) state models accounted 'only for age, sex, and principal components'. Genotyping array/batch not listed as covariate (single Axiom MVP 1.0 array). Post-GWAS QC (SM p.4, EasyQC-based): removed missing/implausible statistics, monomorphic, r2<0.3, MAF<0.0001 variants. Pre-GWAS variant QC (SM p.2): call rate <97.5% (MAF>1%) or <99% (MAF<1%), >10% deviation from 1000G allele frequency excluded. Genomic control 'was implemented for each population' before meta-analysis (SM p.5); whether the released population-specific files carry GC-corrected statistics is not stated. Corroborative check only, not definitive validation ( from rounded allele frequencies): in our EUR CAD file min MAC ~85 over 19,708,268 variants, i.e., the MAF>=0.0001 post-GWAS filter (2N x 0.0001 = 83.5) is binding in EUR.
meta_analysis: None for this file (single-population GIA GWAS). The paper's multi-population GWAMA fixed-effect IVW meta-analysis (SM p.5; GC per population, not on meta) is a separate META file not used here.

ancestry_handling: Finnish-ancestry restriction: sample QC excludes non-Finnish ancestry using PCA with 1000 Genomes plus a Bayesian outlier step, then Mahalanobis-distance probability (threshold 0.95) relative to FIN vs EUR 1kG clusters; twins/duplicates rejected. Related Finnish samples are retained (handbook 'Sample QC and PCA': inliers = unrelated Finnish-ancestry; 'outliers' = non-duplicate Finnish-ancestry samples related to inliers). Relatedness handled by REGENIE whole-genome regression (step 1 LOCO predictions, GRM variant set INFO>0.95 in all batches, >97% non-missing, MAF>1%, LD-pruned 1.5 Mb / r2 0.2; R12 config uses R12_GRM_V0_LD_0.2).
phenotype_preprocessing: Registry-based binary endpoint (DF12 endpoint definition file): hospital discharge (HD) or cause-of-death (COD) codes ICD-10 I70; ICD-9 440, 4370, 4371X; ICD-8 440. Parent I70-I79. No control-exclusion field set (controls = participants without the endpoint). No transformation.
association_model_covariates: REGENIE (R12 pipeline docker regenie 2.2.4_FG), additive model, approximate Firth for variants with initial P<0.01 with SE from effect and LRT p (--firth --approx --pThresh 0.01 --firth-se); MAC>=5 among cases and controls. Covariates (R12 binary config): SEX_IMPUTED, AGE_AT_DEATH_OR_END_OF_FOLLOWUP, PC1-10, IS_FINNGEN2_CHIP, and legacy genotyping BATCH_* indicators; covariates with <10 cases excluded (covariate_inclusion_threshold 10); sex dropped automatically for sex-specific endpoints. Handbook wording: age, sex, 10 PCs, FinnGen 1 or 2 chip or legacy genotyping batch.
meta_analysis: None (single-biobank GWAS).

phenotype_preprocessing: Binary PAD; definitions per study (Supplemental Table I): majority of cases (n=7,172) from clinical parameters (ABI<0.9 at rest or post-exercise, clinical diagnosis, PAD-specific procedures, claudication treatment); n=4,914 cases from self-report with clinical vascular disease evidence and hospital admission codes. ancestry_handling: Population-stratified analysis by genetically inferred ancestry (GIA). Published SM (PDF p.2, 'Population assignment'): 1000 Genomes reference merged with MVP; EIGENSOFT smartpca used to project reference PC loadings; random-forest classifier trained on top 10 reference PCs; individuals assigned to a group if probability >50%, others excluded. Main text p.10 (limitations): the 50% threshold excluded 5,953 participants (<1% of cohort); authors note this may neglect admixture. Groups: AFR, AMR, EAS, EUR (SAS too few cases). Parallel HARE-based GWAS also run (SM p.3) - not the files used here (file N matches GIA Table S2). GWAS run separately within each GIA group; relatedness handled within SAIGE GLMM (SM p.4 'to account for participant relatedness and unbalanced case-control ratios'); SAIGE-GPU builds a full GRM (ref. 48 title); no relative-exclusion step described. PCs: 'PC1-10' selected for adjustment (SM p.2), population-specific (SM p.4). This file: AFR GIA group (genetically similar to 1000G AFR; Table S1 AFR N=121,177); PCs computed within this population. Admixture not modelled beyond the ten population-specific PCs; the authors flag discrete grouping as a limitation (main p.10).
phenotype_preprocessing: Binary phecode from VA EHR ICD-9/ICD-10 codes, follow-up to September 2020 (SM p.2). Published SM p.3 ('Phenotypes from ICD codes'): ICD-9 and ICD-10 codes mapped to 1,876 phecodes (Bastarache 2021, SM ref. 62); case = at least two phecode-mapped ICD-9/ICD-10 codes; control = no instance of a phecode-mapped code; >=200 cases required within each population group; VA-protected conditions (e.g., sickle cell anaemia, HIV) excluded. Table S2: Phe_440_2 'Atherosclerosis of the extremities', cases 4,282 / controls 113,972 (N 118,254) - identical to num_cases/num_controls in our downloaded file. Individuals with exactly one mapped code are by construction neither case nor control. Phecode exclusion ranges for controls are not described; phecode map version (e.g., 1.2 vs X) is not stated. Age definition (enrolment vs last visit) not stated. No transformation (binary).
association_model_covariates: SAIGE (GPU-optimised SAIGE-GPU on OLCF Summit; SM p.4) generalized/logistic mixed model: step 1 on directly genotyped variants, step 2 on imputed dosages (hybrid African Genome Resources + 1000G Phase 3 v5 panel; SM p.2). Variants included: imputation quality >0.3 and MAC >40 within the population group (SM p.4; main text p.3 '>44.3M variants [with minor allele count (MAC) > 40]'). Covariates: 'Analyses were adjusted for age, sex, and ten population-specific genetic PCs' (SM p.4); limitations (main p.10) state models accounted 'only for age, sex, and principal components'. Genotyping array/batch not listed as covariate (single Axiom MVP 1.0 array). Post-GWAS QC (SM p.4, EasyQC-based): removed missing/implausible statistics, monomorphic, r2<0.3, MAF<0.0001 variants. Pre-GWAS variant QC (SM p.2): call rate <97.5% (MAF>1%) or <99% (MAF<1%), >10% deviation from 1000G allele frequency excluded. Genomic control 'was implemented for each population' before meta-analysis (SM p.5); whether the released population-specific files carry GC-corrected statistics is not stated. Corroborative check only, not definitive validation ( from 4-dp rounded allele frequencies): in our AFR file min MAC ~26 with only 9 of 36,970,753 variants at MAC<=40 (rounding error up to ~12 alleles), consistent with MAC>40.
meta_analysis: None for this file (single-population GIA GWAS). The paper's multi-population GWAMA fixed-effect IVW meta-analysis (SM p.5; GC per population, not on meta) is a separate META file not used here.

ancestry_handling: UKB: 456,426 European-ancestry participants assigned by projection onto first two PCs of 1000G HapMap3 SNPs and bivariate-Gaussian assignment to closest super-population; BOLT-LMM mixed model (HM3 model SNPs) for relatedness and stratification. GIANT (Locke 2015): European-descent studies; relatedness handled per study (Locke Supp Table 2).
phenotype_preprocessing: UKB: BMI adjusted for age, sex, 10 PCs, recruitment centre and genotyping batch, residualised separately in males and females, then inverse-normal transformed. GIANT: BMI adjusted for age, age^2 and study-specific covariates (e.g. PCs), residuals computed by sex (and case/control status) in unrelated-sample studies or with sex as covariate in family studies, then inverse-normal transformed.
association_model_covariates: UKB: BOLT-LMM v2.3 on residualised IRNT BMI (covariates entered via residualisation: age, sex, 10 PCs from flashPCA, recruitment centre, genotyping batch). GIANT: per-study linear regression on IRNT residuals, additive model; extra covariates varied by study.
meta_analysis: Fixed-effect inverse-variance-weighted METAL meta of UKB with Locke 2015 GIANT BMI summary statistics (~2.4M HapMap2 SNPs; N~681k average). Covariates varied by cohort in the GIANT component.

ancestry_handling: UKB individuals of European ancestry (N=462,690) via the MRC IEU UKB GWAS pipeline (Elsworth 2017); exclusion details in the paper Supplementary Note (not accessed). Relatedness and stratification handled by BOLT-LMM.
phenotype_preprocessing: Index built from self-reported smoking status, age at initiation, age at cessation and cigarettes/day (Leffondre 2006 method) with half-life tau=18 chosen by simulation against lung cancer and mortality; never smokers included. Not standardised: deposit README says betas are unstandardised (divide beta and SE by SD 0.6940093 to get SD units).
association_model_covariates: BOLT-LMM linear mixed model with genotyping chip and sex as covariates (deposit README: summary statistics adjusted for sex and genotyping chip). Age and PCs not listed. Sensitivity GWAS without chip adjustment described in paper (not the deposited file).
meta_analysis: None (single UKB GWAS).

ancestry_handling: Cohort analyses run separately by ancestry group (EUR, EAS, AFR, HIS, SAS) and stratified by case/control status where relevant; ancestry outliers removed by within-ancestry PCA; PCs of ancestry as covariates. Relatedness: most cohorts used linear mixed models (rvtests, BOLT-LMM, SAIGE or deCODE software).
phenotype_preprocessing: Residuals generated separately in males and females adjusting for age, age^2, PCs of ancestry and study-specific covariates, then inverse-normal transformed. Individuals on cholesterol-lowering medication: pre-medication LDL-C approximated as LDL-C/0.7 (TC/0.8). Fasting status and LDL-C derivation (measured vs calculated) undocumented in sources checked.
association_model_covariates: Association of IRNT residuals with SNPs (covariates entered via residualisation: age, age^2, PCs, study-specific covariates); sex-stratified results or sex-combined with sex as covariate. Software mostly rvtests mixed models. Number of PCs and extra covariates varied by cohort (GWAS protocol: Protocol Exchange doi:10.21203/rs.3.pex-1687/v1, not opened).
meta_analysis: Ancestry-specific: RAREMETAL; trans-ancestry discovery: MR-MEGA with 5 axes of genetic variation; effect sizes from fixed-effects METAL. The downloaded trans-ancestry file carries METAL_Effect/StdErr (fixed-effects IVW) plus MR-MEGA p-values. Cohort-level GC correction applied. Covariates varied by cohort.

ancestry_handling: European ancestry only: UKB self-reported European-ancestry participants; MVP self-reported non-Hispanic white; BioVU unrelated self-reported European-ancestry adults; ICBP studies of European descent. Relatedness: UKB BOLT-LMM mixed model; BioVU restricted to unrelated; MVP and ICBP per study (not detailed).
phenotype_preprocessing: Treated-BP correction: +15 mmHg to SBP (+10 DBP) if on antihypertensive medication, in UKB, ICBP studies, MVP and BioVU. UKB: mean of two automated or manual readings; pregnant women excluded. MVP/BioVU: median outpatient SBP from EHR, excluding measures at/after CKD, secondary hypertension or heart-failure codes (and pain score >=5 in MVP). Untransformed (mmHg).
association_model_covariates: All studies: linear regression adjusted for age at BP measurement, age^2, sex, BMI and top 10 PCs. UKB: BOLT-LMM v2.3; MVP and BioVU: SNPTEST v2.5.4; ICBP: per-study models (77 studies, meta-analysed beforehand).
meta_analysis: Inverse-variance-weighted fixed-effects METAL meta-analysis of the four datasets after LDSC-intercept correction of UKB, MVP and BioVU (ICBP already GC-corrected; ICBP itself IVW METAL across 77 studies). Covariate set common by design; ICBP study-level specifics not detailed.

notes: SBP is BMI-adjusted: relevant for mediation analyses that also include BMI (possible collider bias). Per-study details came from the preprint; the published XML did not restate them. File N=1,009,750 at first row vs 1,028,980 total.

ancestry_handling: 122 GWAS from five ancestry groups (EUR 51.1%, EAS 28.4%, SAS 8.3%, AFR 6.6%, HIS 5.6% of Neff); each ancestry-specific GWAS imputed separately. Structure/relatedness handled per study by either excluding relatives and adjusting for GRM-derived PCs, or a GRM random effect in a mixed model; study-level genomic control if lambda>1.
phenotype_preprocessing: Case/control T2D; definitions per study in Supplementary Tables 1-3 (not accessed) - undocumented in sources checked. Linear(mixed)-model effects converted to log-odds scale.
association_model_covariates: Additive model on minor-allele dosage adjusted for age and sex (where appropriate) plus study-specific covariates (Supp Table 4, not accessed). BMI adjustment not stated in the main text (paper cites BMI-adjusted analyses only for earlier EUR/EAS components).
meta_analysis: Primary: MR-MEGA meta-regression with 3 axes of genetic variation. Also fixed-effects IVW METAL and random-effects METASOFT. Downloaded DIAMANTE-TA file provides MR-MEGA p-values and Fixed-effects_beta/SE (METAL). Covariates varied by study.
